brownfield.boundary: Recorded maintenance observations in one familiar private repository; not an independent benchmark or general portability proof.

comparisons.focus: Structured specifications, planning, implementation and convergence; extensible processes for coding agents.
comparisons.name: GitHub Spec Kit
comparisons.relationship: Overlaps in structured context and process guidance. Compare the concrete workflow and extension set you need; no blanket claim of absent governance.

comparisons.focus: Installs and runs configured multi-language Git hooks.
comparisons.name: pre-commit
comparisons.relationship: Useful alongside Kit gates. Hook execution and the Kit's repository-state, handoff and release contracts address different layers.

comparisons.focus: Agent tool execution with documented run modes, approvals and sandboxing controls.
comparisons.name: Cursor
comparisons.relationship: Overlaps in execution safety. A coding executor can use Kit commands; no measured productivity, safety or cost ranking is claimed.

comparisons.focus: Coding assistance and agent workflows, including a cloud agent that can create branches, write code and open pull requests.
comparisons.name: GitHub Copilot
comparisons.relationship: Overlaps in development and PR workflows. Kit contracts can be an additional repository layer; compatibility with every product mode is not claimed.

greenfield.boundary: Historical released-package first-cycle work/PR/CI/merge/handoff retest in a private external repository; not a retest of every later release.

notes: Let transfer order-create write command orders: --run-command '<argv>' is checked against the command manifest when the order is created, flags commands that need the local --allow-unlisted, refuses commands no flag could allow, and an order's agentic-kit commands run with the workspace's own Kit instead of whatever PATH finds (KIT-GF-074).

Publish what a transfer order produced: after the order ran, transfer remote-next commits the files its write actions wrote, its command-run report and LATEST_COMMAND_RUN.txt together with its report, so the checkout ends clean on the transfer branch; changes the order did not declare are never published and turn the result BLOCKED (KIT-GF-075).

Stop counting the .gitkeep carriers that workspace init writes into the transfer inbox and outbox as obsolete transfer files, which blocked every transfer remote-next of a freshly initialized workspace (KIT-GF-076).

Accept a consumer's light-path checks as SKIPPED only on a light pull request: a workspace names them under gates.light_path_skipped_checks in .agentic/config.yaml, and pr wait-ci, PR status, merge-if-green and post-merge settlement accept them when the Kit re-derives the ci runtime-plan classification of the pull request as light; on a full pull request, or when nothing is declared, a skipped check still blocks (KIT-GF-073).

Let kit update maintain every Kit pin of the managed CI file, so a separate classify job beside the gate job is updated too; all pins must name the same exact version on their own pip install line (KIT-GF-071).

Scope the external rule-mechanism inventory's surface evidence to the lines carrying its anchor instead of whole files, so unrelated edits of .agentic/config.yaml or the rules README keep rule-registry check PASS (inventory schema 2; a schema 1 inventory is refreshed by bootstrap), and let a signed kit update re-derive a Kit-derived inventory with the updated Kit; a hand-reviewed inventory is never touched (KIT-GF-072).
